dovevo.en: I had to; I had to

texto: It serves to describe continued situations, physical or mood states, and habits in the past. It is equivalent to the Spanish imperfect pretérito («I was», «I was talking.», «I lived.»).
Unlike the prossimo passage, the imperfect does not indicate when the action ended and does not present it as a closed fact.

The root of the infinitive is taken and the disinences are added: **-avo, -avi, -ava, -avamo, -avate, -avano** for -are (* parlavo *); **-evo, -evi, -eva, -evamo, -evate, -evano** for -ere (* leggevo *); **-ivo, -ivi, -iva, -ivamo, -ivate, -ivano** for -ire (* dormant *).

**Essere**: * ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano *. **Fare**: * facevo, facevi, faceva, facevamo, facevate, facevano *. **Dire**: * dicevo, dicevi, diceva... *. **Bere**: * bevevo, bevevi, beveva... *

frases.en: When you were little, where did you live?

frases.it: Abitavo a Milano, con i miei genitori.
frases.es: Vivía en Milán, con mis padres.
frases.en: I lived in Milan, with my parents.

frases.it: Giocavo a calcio e leggevo molto.
frases.es: Jugaba al fútbol y leía mucho.
frases.en: He played football and read a lot.

frases.it: Davvero? Io invece parlavo sempre con tutti!
frases.es: ¿De verdad? ¡Yo en cambio hablaba siempre con todos!
frases.en: Really? I was always talking to everyone instead!

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «I was talking.» in Italian in time imfet?

opciones.explicacion: The first regular person of the verbs in -are ends in -avo.
It expresses a timely action concluded in prossimo passage.
This is the form of an indicative present.

bloques.pregunta: What is the form of a «I was / I was» imperfect?

opciones.explicacion: «Essere» presents its own forms of imperfect: ero, eri, was...
Compound form of perfect plascuamperfect (trapassate).
It corresponds to the present indicative.

bloques.frase: Quando ___ piccolo, giocavo molto fuori casa.

opciones.explicacion: With the first person subject singular corresponds «ero».
Second person singular («tu»).
Third person singular («lui / lei»).

bloques.frase: Abitavo a Madrid quando ero studente.

opciones.texto: He lived in Madrid when he was a student.
opciones.explicacion: «Abitavo» describes a regular and prolonged situation in the past.

opciones.texto: I've lived in Madrid this last month.
opciones.explicacion: It refers to a continuous stage in imperfect, not a recent period of delimited.

opciones.texto: I'll live in Madrid when I finish my studies.
opciones.explicacion: It expresses the usual past, not the future.

bloques.pregunta: What habit of the past does prayer express?
bloques.frase: Di solito dormivo molto la domenica mattina.

opciones.texto: I usually slept a lot on Sundays in the morning.
opciones.explicacion: «Di solito» indicates regularity combined with the imperfect «dormivo».

opciones.texto: I slept too late yesterday morning.
opciones.explicacion: It describes a usual custom, not an isolated fact of a specific day.

opciones.texto: I sleep a lot of hours every weekend.
opciones.explicacion: The action belongs to the past, not to the usual present.

bloques.traduccion: When I was little I always played.
bloques.explicacion: The usual structure in imperfect with «quando» and frequency warning.

bloques.frase: Quando abitavo a Roma, ___ spesso con gli amici.

opciones.explicacion: «Parlavo» is the first regular person of «parlare» in imperfect.
This is the form of an indicative present.
It would indicate a single conversation over.

bloques.pregunta: What form is «We were» in imperfect?

opciones.explicacion: First person from the plural of the verb «essere» in imperfect.
This is the form of an indicative present.
It means «We have», the verb is broken.

intro: To describe what things were like, childhood or what you were usually doing in the past, Italian uses «imperfetto».
